scope: Manuscript mathematical dependencies; the active audit concerns M_EXACT and its ancestors, not a proof of the remaining global construction.

M_MAIN.statement: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into R^4 (introduction.tex, thm:main).

M_GLOBAL_PREPARATION.statement: A finite ordered primitive decomposition and spherical starting immersion satisfy every prescribed intermediate Hessian and boundary condition (global-construction.tex, lem:global-preparation).

M_SPHERICAL_PREPARATION.statement: The spherical second form can be killed at an arbitrary finite set with uniform C^2 and metric bounds (global-construction.tex, lem:spherical-preparation).

M_ORDINARY_IMMERSION.statement: Whitney's ordinary immersion theorem supplies a starting immersion of a closed surface into R^3; manuscript citation Whitney1944, Theorem 8.

M_REGULAR_VALUES.statement: The stated applications of Sard's theorem supply regular support boundaries and avoid multiple crossings; manuscript citation Sard1942, Theorem 4.1.

M_PRIMITIVE_ADDITION.statement: A positive primitive metric addition can be realized while preserving nonzero second form, a preferred normal, and all later boundary conditions (primitive-statement.tex, prop:primitive-addition).

M_VELOCITY_LOOP.statement: A smooth periodic velocity loop has the prescribed norm, mean, flat support extension, and turn inequalities (velocity-loop.tex, lem:velocity-loop).

M_VELOCITY_PLANE.statement: The transverse Hessian condition supplies the nondegenerate velocity plane and local frame (velocity-loop.tex, lem:velocity-plane).

M_LOOP_DENSITY.statement: Smooth positive circle densities realize the required interior averages (velocity-loop.tex, lem:loop-density).

M_SMALL_VALUE_DERIVATIVE.statement: Small-value phase modifications prescribe large transverse derivatives at the finitely many turns (velocity-loop.tex, lem:small-value-derivative).

M_PRIMITIVE_REALIZATION.statement: The velocity loop admits an exact smooth realization with the stated first/second derivative asymptotics and uniformly nonzero second form (primitive-realization.tex, prop:primitive-realization).

M_FINITE_PERIODIC_EXPANSION.statement: Finite periodic differential correctors remove every requested oscillatory order, leaving polynomial-above-order-two mean operators (primitive-realization.tex, lem:finite-periodic-expansion).

M_REALIZATION_NONZERO.statement: The transverse limiting second form stays uniformly nonzero before exact correction (primitive-realization.tex, final subsection).

M_GEOMETRY_PRESERVATION.statement: Exact Gauss identities and turn bounds preserve the ordered crossing inequalities and permit the global preferred normal to be joined (geometry-preservation.tex).

M_GAUSS.statement: The Euclidean Gauss equation and its crossing-invariant reformulation have the displayed signs (preliminaries.tex, eq:gauss; primitive-statement.tex, eq:crossing-gauss-interpretation).

M_EXACT.statement: Finite polynomial input jets, a sufficiently small finite-order metric defect, and a uniformly nonzero second form suffice for smooth exact correction with o(1) C^2 displacement; R,N are independent of implicit input constants (exact-correction.tex, prop:exact-correction).

M_PHASE_DATA.statement: Positive rank-one phase decompositions have good individual, doubled, and pairwise sum/difference phases (preliminaries.tex, lem:phase-data).

M_POLYNOMIAL_PHASE_DATA.statement: Varying-family phase data, inverse coframes, reciprocal second-form lengths, and all fixed-order derivatives have polynomial z bounds on a persistent C^2 neighborhood (preliminaries.tex, lem:polynomial-phase-data).

M_SMALL_INCREMENT.statement: Finite-mode corrections add delta^2 H with error O_tau(delta eta^q + delta^3/tau); fixed output norms and thresholds use finitely many input norms (small-modes.tex, prop:small-increment).

M_SMALL_UNPERTURBED.statement: The unperturbed case P=gamma of prop:small-increment has finite-jet domain thresholds independent of the output observation order.

M_PERTURBED_MODE_MEAN.statement: The polynomially perturbed operator has the required finite-mode and mean-difference estimates, with no q-dependent perturbation power (small-modes.tex). This extension is outside the unperturbed audit.

M_MODE_PARAMETRIX.statement: For the unperturbed metric map, eliminating the yy normal equation leaves a first-order tangential system and a finite support-preserving parametrix with a small residual (small-modes.tex, eq:normal-elimination through eq:finite-free-mode).

M_MEAN_ADJUSTMENT.statement: For the unperturbed metric map, the quadratic mean is delta^2(A+T(A)); finite substitutions improve the mean error despite a finite derivative loss (small-modes.tex, eq:quadratic-mean-map through eq:adjusted-quadratic-mean).

M_CUBIC_CONTROL.statement: For the unperturbed metric map, cancelling nonzero quadratic modes leaves an error bounded by delta^3/tau and keeps the segment in the admissible low-jet domain (small-modes.tex, final proof subsection).

M_PERTURBATION_POWER.statement: For fixed polynomial-above-order-two perturbations, p=E+6 controls variations through degree three independently of q (small-modes.tex, eq:fixed-perturbation-power). The unperturbed exact-correction case does not need this extra assertion.

M_SMOOTHING.statement: Moment-cancelling smoothing has finite-order approximation and all-order derivative bounds; the unsmoothed high-input tail is linear (exact-correction.tex, lem:finite-order-smoothing and eq:exact-smoothing-tail).

M_LINEAR_TAIL.statement: The quadratic metric identity contains no square of G-S_sG: delta'^2(H'-h*)=delta^2(H-H_s)-E-C(G-G_s,U) (exact-correction.tex, eq:exact-error-identity).

M_EXACT_STEP.statement: A single smoothed increment satisfies the all-order linear true-input recurrence with thresholds independent of uncontrolled higher derivatives (exact-correction.tex, lem:exact-step).

M_INITIALIZATION.statement: R=440 and a sufficiently large N initialize the first block at t=z^mu, independently of implicit input constants (exact-correction.tex, initialization subsection).

M_FINITE_WAITING.statement: The all-order recurrence yields finite waiting times, increasing retained derivative order, smooth convergence, and the total C^2 displacement estimate (exact-correction.tex, final subsection).

C_POLY_CORRECTION.statement: For every D>=4 and a,b,d>=0,L>0, finite jets through order 442, uniformly elliptic varying targets, defect O(z^N), and transverse second form >=c z^d suffice for smooth exact correction with C^2 displacement <=z^L, for a constant-independent finite N (research/exact_correction_audit/theorem.md).

C_FINITE_WAIT_CORE.statement: The scalar all-order recurrence has arbitrarily late finite hitting times below B for every finite initial value; the metric-transfer identity and increment exponent margin hold universally.
